copy.title: The Walton Money File
copy.desc: An interactive, fully sourced map of the Walton family: who owns what, which stock you can buy, the Broncos deal, and the money on the public record.
copy.eyebrow: File #014 · The Walton family · Data as of
copy.h1: America’s richest family still owns 44% of Walmart. We followed the money.
copy.lede: Who’s who, what each of them owns, which of their companies you can buy stock in, and the money on the public record. Every number links to its source.
copy.familyLede: Tap anyone to open their file: what they own, what’s on the record, and where every fact comes from. Grandchildren who aren’t public figures are left out.
copy.investLede: One family company trades on the stock market: Walmart. The bank, the football team and the rest are privately owned.
copy.moneyLede: Nearly all of it is Walmart stock, held together through Walton Enterprises. Forbes puts the whole family at $520 billion. Four people on this map have their own published net worth.
copy.recordLede: The money that shows up in SEC filings, deals and gifts. Filings and reporting, not guesses.
copy.trailLede: From a five-and-dime in Newport, Arkansas, in 1945 to the richest family in America.

summary.t: Sam Walton’s eldest son. Chairman of Walmart from 1992 to 2015 and a director until 2024. In 2022 he led the group that bought the Denver Broncos.

owns.t: Held 7.03 million Walmart shares (0.09%) in his own name in early 2026. Most of the family’s stake sits inside Walton Enterprises. Since December 2024 four family trusts have run it, and Rob is a trustee of one of them.
Led the Walton-Penner group that bought the team for a record $4.65 billion in 2022, with his daughter Carrie and son-in-law Greg.

record.t: Named chairman on April 7, 1992, two days after his father died. Greg Penner, his son-in-law, replaced him in 2015. He left Walmart’s board in 2024.

On December 18, 2024, Rob, Jim, Alice and John’s estate trust moved their managing interests in Walton Enterprises to four family trusts that act by majority vote. Eight more family members, including Carrie and Lukas, became trustees of the Walton Family Holdings Trust.

facts.t: The AP put his worth at about $60 billion when he bought the Broncos, which made him the NFL’s richest owner at the time.
Forbes puts the whole Walton family at $520 billion, three times the next-richest family, the Kochs.

kidsNote.t: Rob has three children. His daughter Carrie and her husband, Greg Penner, are on this map.

summary.t: Sam’s youngest son. Chairman of the family’s Arvest Bank Group. He sat on Walmart’s board for more than a decade, then gave the seat to his son Steuart in 2016.

owns.t: Held 31.5 million Walmart shares (0.40%) in his own name in early 2026, the most of any family member listed in the filing.
Chairman of the family’s bank, which has $28 billion in assets.

record.t: Has pledged 3.22 million of his Walmart shares as collateral for lines of credit extended to a company not affiliated with Walmart.

facts.t: His daughter Annie Proietti chairs the Walton Family Foundation, which had $8.6 billion in assets in 2024.

summary.t: Sam’s only daughter. She stayed off Walmart’s board and focused on art and giving. She founded the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville in 2011 and opened a medical school there in 2025.

owns.t: Held 20.2 million Walmart shares (0.25%) in her own name in early 2026.

record.t: Paid the museum’s $320 million construction bill. By 2015 the Waltons had put $800 million into its endowment.
Bought Asher Durand’s painting Kindred Spirits from the New York Public Library in 2005 for a reported $35 million.
The Alice L. Walton School of Medicine opened in Bentonville in 2025 with a first class of 48 students.

facts.t: Crystal Bridges is free to visit.

summary.t: Sam and Helen’s second son. A Green Beret medic in Vietnam who received the Silver Star. He later chaired a venture capital firm and in 1998 co-founded the Children’s Scholarship Fund, which helps low-income families pay private-school tuition. He died in a plane crash in Wyoming in 2005.

worth.none: No current estimate. He died in 2005.

owns.t: Got 20% of the family partnership in 1953. His estate trust stayed a managing member of Walton Enterprises until December 2024.

record.t: His son Lukas received about one third of his estate and his widow, Christy Walton, about one sixth.

facts.t: Forbes had estimated his net worth at $18.2 billion when he died, fourth-richest in the U.S.

summary.t: Opened the first Walmart in Rogers, Arkansas, in 1962, at 44. Took the company public in 1970. He died in 1992, shortly after receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

worth.none: No current estimate. He died in 1992.

owns.t: Founder. In 1953 he set up the family business as a partnership, giving each of his four children 20% while he and Helen kept 20%.

facts.t: He wrote in his memoir that the transfer happened so early that the family “didn’t have to pay substantial gift or inheritance taxes on it.”
Walmart’s first public shares sold for $16.50 each in 1970.
Before Walmart, he opened Walton’s 5&10 on the Bentonville town square in 1950.

summary.t: Married Sam in 1943. They opened their first store together, a Ben Franklin variety store in Newport, Arkansas, in 1945. Sam credited her with the idea for Walmart’s profit-sharing plan.

worth.none: No current estimate. She died in 2007.

record.t: As president of the Walton Family Foundation, she oversaw its $300 million gift to the University of Arkansas in 2002.

facts.t: When Sam died in 1992, he left his Walmart ownership to Helen and their four children.

summary.t: Rob’s daughter. She sits on the Walton Family Foundation board, is an Aspen Institute trustee and backs charter schools. She co-owns the Broncos with her father and her husband, Greg Penner.

owns.t: Held 1.45 million Walmart shares in her own name in early 2026. A trustee of the Walton Family Holdings Trust since December 2024.
Her and Greg’s family company. In April 2026 it made an investment that will make it the largest minority owner of the Colorado Rockies.

summary.t: Married to Rob’s daughter, Carrie. Chairman of Walmart since 2015, only the third person in the job after Sam and Rob. Also CEO of the Denver Broncos.

owns.t: Joined the board in 2008 and became chairman in 2015. Earlier he was CFO of Walmart Japan and ran finance and strategy for Walmart.com.
Owner and CEO. The team lists him as the designated controlling owner of the Walton-Penner Family Ownership Group.
Founder and general partner of the investment firm.
In April 2026 his and Carrie’s family company made an investment that will make it the largest minority owner of the Colorado Rockies.

facts.t: He met Carrie when they were undergraduates at Georgetown.
Walmart’s 2026 proxy says only two Walton family members serve on its board, even though family entities hold about 44% of the shares.

summary.t: Sam Walton’s grandson. He inherited about a third of his father John’s estate in 2005. He owns stakes in Walmart and Arvest Bank but works for neither, and runs Builders Vision, a sustainability-focused giving and impact-investing platform.

owns.t: Held 902,822 Walmart shares in his own name in early 2026. Since December 2024 he has been the trustee of one of the four family trusts that run Walton Enterprises.
Owns a stake in the family’s bank.
Founded it in 2021. It has handed out more than $3 billion.

record.t: One of eight family members who became trustees of the Walton Family Holdings Trust in December 2024.
